items.method: Cross-read the market-heatmap breadth percentage against its 60% threshold and against the benchmark's distance from its 52-week high and its moving-average stack, then overlay the option-flow call fraction and put-versus-call premium and the VIX band to judge whether an index holding near its high is being carried by a set of leaders that has narrowed but not collapsed.
items.note: A mild narrow-leadership divergence carries into the pre-market window. The SPY benchmark last printed 767.45, only 1.34% under its 52-week high, in a bull-stacked moving-average regime (50-day distance +2.39%, 200-day +9.07%, 126-day momentum +12.99%), yet just 55.23% of the 134 market-heatmap constituents are positive on the day — a 4.77-point shortfall to the 60% broad-participation threshold. Premium flow is not confirming the strength: it reads put-heavy and defensive, with calls only 39.9% of premium (about $1.43B of call premium against $2.15B of puts) across 12 tickers and 1730 flagged contracts. VIX 15.73 keeps this in a calm, pressure-not-panic band, while swing structure now reads bull-stacked with an active, qualified double-top pattern over 520 bars. A headline index pinned near its high on roughly 55% breadth, with hedging premium leading and a double top forming overhead, is a milder version of the thinning-leadership pattern: participation is broader than a deep divergence but still under the healthy line. What to watch is whether breadth re-broadens back above the 60% threshold or the tape converges down toward the narrower leaders.
items.title: SPY holds about 1.3% under its 52-week high in a bull-stacked regime while daily breadth stalls just below 60% and premium flow leans put-heavy

inputs: options-structure-lab.regime=negative; signedNetGEX=-3.39B; flip=770.48; callWall=768; putWall=767; expectedMove=2.23; spot=767.79; atmIV=0.0785
options-flow-feed-lab.notable=SPY 768P $66.3M (222.5x OI, same-day); AMD 480C $8.0M (1DTE, 7.6x OI); MSFT 485C $7.65M; lean=put-heavy
items.method: Read the options-structure signed net-gamma sign with its flip and wall levels against current spot, size the expected-move band, confirm the dealer scenario and hold from the gamma playbook, then overlay the most-unusual option prints and the intraday session type and VWAP to judge whether short-gamma dealers are positioned to accelerate a break of the nearest wall.
items.note: Dealer positioning and price have converged on a pinched gamma corridor this window. Signed net gamma is negative at about -$3.39B, and SPY spot 767.79 sits below the 770.48 flip, wedged between the 767 put wall and the 768 call wall. The front expected move is a tight plus or minus 2.23 across three priced expiries, so both walls bracket spot inside a narrow band. Under negative gamma dealers hedge in the direction of the move, so sustained pressure at a wall tends to extend rather than mean-revert. The flow tape agrees at the level: among the most unusual prints is a same-day SPY 768 put at $66.3M on 222.5x open interest, printed right at the call wall, alongside a 1-day AMD 480 call at $8.0M on 7.6x open interest and an MSFT 485 call at $7.65M. The live auction is a range day under mixed control with VWAP 768.08 just above spot after a 0.52% gap-down open. This is a coiled range-break-watch structure with a patient, same-session-fade playbook: while 767 holds and VIX 15.73 stays calm it can stay orderly, but a sustained loss of the 767 put wall in short-gamma is what would tip the balance toward downside acceleration rather than a fade.
items.title: SPY spot rests between the 767 put wall and 768 call wall below the 770.48 negative-gamma flip as the same-day tape sells a $66M SPY 768 put
